key_insight: Oxide-cap size and position alter aluminum-particle combustion: front caps enhance local evaporation near the cap–metal junction, while rear caps absorb heat and lower reaction temperatures.
engineering_relevance: Cap-aware evaporation and drag models can improve Lagrangian predictions of burning aluminum particles without resolving each particle’s boundary layer.
method: Boundary-layer resolved simulations varying cap size, cap position, and particle Reynolds number.
Film properties estimated using a 0.55-rule for temperature, species mass fractions, and pressure.
Optimized Whitaker evaporation and Schiller–Naumann drag correlations, with extensions to capped doublet particles.
evidence_signal: The optimized correlations agreed well with the simulations; exposed aluminum area supported rear-cap evaporation predictions, but front caps required an additional mass-flux correction, especially at high particle Reynolds numbers.
watch_item: The abstract reports simulation-based agreement without quantitative errors or experimental validation, leaving accuracy outside the studied conditions uncertain.
paper_title: Influence of an oxide cap on the combustion of aluminum particles using boundary-layer resolved simulations
